critical.issue: 500 Internal Server Error for users whose profile field is null (freshly registered users). MongoDB rejects $set on 'profile.name' when profile is null. This blocks the App Store account-deletion requirement for any user who has not completed the profile onboarding step. Fix: set the whole 'profile' subdocument (e.g. {"profile": {"name": "Cuenta eliminada"}}) or use two-stage update, or $set only when profile exists. File: /app/backend/routers/auth.py:170-176.

rca_of_issue: DELETE /api/auth/account uses `db.users.update_one({...}, {"$set": {..., "profile.name": "Cuenta eliminada", ...}})`. Fresh users created via POST /auth/register have `profile: None` in Mongo (see register() in routers/auth.py:78). MongoDB's dotted-path $set can only set a nested field if the parent path is a document; it cannot create a field inside `null`. Result: `pymongo.errors.WriteError: Cannot create field 'name' in element {profile: null}` → 500 to the client. Fix: replace the whole subdocument with `"profile": {"name": "Cuenta eliminada"}` in the $set payload (still soft-deletes and anonymises the user, and works for both null-profile and existing-profile users). Reproduction: register a new user with random email + Sentinel2026!, DELETE /api/auth/account with that bearer → 500.
